hero_intro_headline: From one idea to a shippable content pipeline
hero_intro_desc: Video, drama, and image take shape in SuperCool first. When prompts must become searchable assets, signals need to feed operations, or stories need structure—extension modules pick up the handoff without locking you to a single canvas.
hero_desc: Schedules and tooling choices shouldn’t choke imagination. SuperCool threads script, boards, frames, and finals in one workflow—then connects knowledge bases, signal tracking, or multi-agent scripts when you are ready.
about_title: Creation should extend—not stop because a tool ran out of road.
about_desc: Most teams are not short on ideas—they lose time to tool-hopping and handoffs. Pysdn splits generation from modular assets: motion starts on the canvas while knowledge, signals, and scripts compound underneath as searchable, reusable layers. Ideas grow into versions, paths, and shippable work instead of living only in your head or chat logs.
about_stat_models: Major models ready to plug in
about_pain_1: Jumping across 5+ tools fragments the flow
about_pain_3: Uneven output quality; delivery feels like luck
about_pain_4: Characters and style drift the moment the project changes
about_gain_1: One surface for generate, refine, and trace end to end
about_gain_2: Git-like version trees you can rewind anytime
about_gain_4: Lock voices/roles and reuse style libraries across projects

forge_desc: Forge is SuperCool’s prompt and output knowledge module. It does not generate media itself, but structures prompts, versions, parameters, and results into a searchable relational system.
forge_f1: Standardize prompts / generations / tags / versions into one schema.
forge_f2: Store only request_id, model_version, output_url, and sync status back through webhooks.
forge_f3: Combine PostgreSQL GIN, full-text search, and pgvector for semantic recall and multi-filter queries.
forge_f4: Track Prompt VersionTree, AI tag inference, and one-click reuse in the same loop.
forge_f5: Keep CDN/S3 links, thumbnails, frame extraction, and metadata parsing while originals stay external.
forge_flow_caption: Store metadata, request_id, model_version, and output_url only. Generation stays in external systems.
track_desc: Track is SuperCool’s web monitoring module. It follows the loop from entity to content to prompt, then feeds strong public signals back into reusable content assets.
track_f1: Standardize entities / accounts / metrics with support for multi-account and parent-child mappings.
track_f2: Collect public data with resilient crawling, rotation, and normalization before metrics.
track_f3: Store follower, engagement, and reach estimates in TimescaleDB with hourly and daily aggregation.
track_f4: AlertEngine triggers webhook or email on growth spikes, negative sentiment, and keyword anomalies.
track_f5: High-performing posts are structured by LLM and written back to SuperForge as prompt templates.
track_flow_caption: Track public data, clean it into entities and time-series signals, then write high-value content back to SuperForge.

tune_desc: SuperTune helps refine prompts, tune parameters, compare variants, and keep cost and latency under control.
tune_f1: PromptRefine: clean structure, negative-term hints, and model-specific formatting.
tune_f2: ParamAutoTune: suggest seeds, steps, guidance, and duration with side-by-side checks.
tune_f3: BatchMacro: run CSV/JSON batches with retries, status, and exports.
tune_f4: QueryCache + CostOptimizer: cache hot prompts and watch cost/latency trends.
tune_f5: FeedbackLoop: learn from edits and nudge templates toward what your team prefers.

workflow_title: Four checkpoints from idea to launch—AI generation plus optional extension modules
workflow_desc: Video, shorts, and images take shape in the SuperCool core first; anchor, sprint, compound, then ship—then attach SuperForge, SuperScript, SuperTrack, and more only when you need them, so ideas become shippable assets without a big-bang rollout.
workflow_interactive_hint: Click the generation-flow timeline or a card below to highlight that phase. Use ‹ › to move between steps—the timeline buttons are keyboard-focusable.
workflow_s1_b1: 🔸 Audience × channels × KPIs on one page
workflow_s1_b2: 🔸 Approval chain × freeze points locked early
workflow_s1_b3: 🔸 Compliance × rights × tone cleared up front
workflow_s1_expand: Compress audience, channels, and KPIs into a one-page consensus brief; lock approval and freeze points before production drags; pre-clear compliance, rights, and brand tone to avoid late rework.
workflow_s2_b1: 🔸 Layout / VO / pacing—many variants, fast reads
workflow_s2_expand: Run parallel variants on the SuperCool core; every drop ships with a share link and a tight note; converge on an upload-ready master and one naming scheme for derivatives and localizations.
workflow_s3_b1: 🔸 SuperForge prompts / style cards on tap
workflow_s3_b3: 🔸 SuperTrack heat / data feeds the next bet
workflow_s3_expand: SuperForge centralizes prompts and style cards for instant reuse; SuperScript keeps boards, scripts, and notes synced to edit, VO, and media buying; SuperTrack / SuperTune loops signals and performance back into the next creative hypothesis.
workflow_s4_expand: Export cross-channel-ready specs for resolution, captions, and codecs; run a final pre-flight on cover, title, and legal lines; close with a light retro and promote winning templates so the next cycle ships faster.
faq_desc: Common questions below—if your case is unique, drop details in the form and we’ll respond in priority order.
faq_1_q: Do I need the backend API to use the site?
faq_1_a: Dev mode can proxy to a local API. You can browse UI and docs without it. For form intake or live stats, point the frontend at the right environment when you’re ready.
faq_2_q: Which languages are supported? Is my choice remembered?
faq_2_a: Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean. Use the language menu or URL params—your choice travels with shared links for collaborators.
faq_3_q: Do I have to enable every extension module?
faq_3_a: No. Start with the modules that match your pain points—e.g., prompt libraries or trend tracking—and expand later to avoid a big-bang rollout.
faq_4_q: Can we run on a private network or self-host?
faq_4_a: We can evaluate deployment models against security and compliance needs. Note identity, logging, and data residency requirements in the form so we can respond with a fit.
faq_5_q: How are rights and usage scoped for generated assets?
faq_5_a: Commercial engagements usually spell out license scope, derivative works, and redistribution in contract. Share your legal template if you have one—we’ll align fast on deliverables.
faq_6_q: How long from first contact to kicking off work?
faq_6_a: It depends on scope. A recommended plan and milestone sketch often lands within about a week after the first working session. Custom integrations, procurement, or security reviews extend the timeline—share your target launch date in the form so we can be realistic.
faq_7_q: Can we start with advisory or training only?
faq_7_a: Yes. Many teams begin with a workflow audit plus templates or a playbook workshop. Your crew can execute internally while we advise on the hardest gaps—note “advisory-only” or “training-first” in your message.
faq_8_q: Who supplies model vendors or API keys?
faq_8_a: Either model works. You can bring your own cloud account and keys so requests stay in your tenant, or we can quote managed capacity. Mention “BYO API vs. managed” and a rough usage band (monthly clips, image count, peak concurrency) so estimates stay honest.
faq_9_q: How is customer data handled—retention, access, and deletion?
faq_9_a: We align with your policy: typical setups scope logs and metadata to the agreed environment, restrict access by role, and support deletion requests per contract. Note retention targets and jurisdictions in the form so we can map controls.
faq_10_q: What support channels do you offer after go-live?
faq_10_a: Email and scheduled calls are standard; higher-tier plans can add a shared channel or response-time windows. For production incidents, describe your escalation path and on-call expectations—we’ll align runbooks and SLAs where applicable.
faq_11_q: Can multiple teams collaborate with roles and approvals?
faq_11_a: Yes. Designs often include project spaces, reviewer roles, and optional approval gates before publish. Tell us your org habits (e.g., brand vs. performance teams) so we don’t over-build workflow.
faq_12_q: What formats and handoffs do you support for creative tools?
faq_12_a: Exports commonly cover timelines, shot lists, stills, and text bundles; integrations vary by stack. Note your preferred tools (e.g., Premiere, DaVinci, Figma) and whether you need API webhooks vs. file drops.
faq_13_q: Is a pilot or proof-of-concept available before a full rollout?
faq_13_a: Often yes—scoped timeboxes with clear success metrics work best. Share audience size, asset types, and what “done” means for your pilot; we’ll propose a minimal footprint and cutover checkpoint.
faq_14_q: How do you handle brand safety and content policy?
faq_14_a: We can layer allow/deny lists, human review steps, and logging for disputed outputs. Specify regulated industries or platform rules (e.g., minors, medical claims) up front so safeguards match your risk profile.
faq_15_q: How does billing and invoicing work—currency and tax?
faq_15_a: Invoices are usually issued per milestone or subscription term; currency and tax treatment follow your entity and region. Mention billing entity, PO process, and tax IDs early to avoid rework.
faq_16_q: How can we influence the roadmap or request features?
faq_16_a: We triage feedback from active partnerships first. Share prioritized use cases and volume signals; roadmap items may ship as beta flags before GA. A short Loom or one-pager often speeds alignment.
